title: Australian police hunt ‘absolute jerk’ who attacked iconic ancient tree with chainsaw | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

Police in WesternAustraliaare looking for the “absolute jerk” who took a chainsaw to acenturies-old treein a “senseless” act of vandalism, local politicians have said.

King Jarrah, which is believed to be between 300 to 500 years old, surviving bush fires and storms, is one of the largest jarrah trees in Wellington National Park, south of Perth, standing at 36 meters tall, or 118 feet, according to the park.

The reserve put out an alert on Tuesday that it would be closing its King Jarrah site and parking lot “due to safety concerns after a tree was vandalised,” and that the area would “remain closed until deemed safe for visitors.”

“In an act that I can only describe as appalling, senseless, and heartbreaking, some absolute jerk has seen fit to vandalise the Wellington National Park’s iconic King Jarrah Tree with a chainsaw!” Matthew Swinbourn, minister for the environment of Western Australia, said Thursday in a jointposton Facebook with Jodie Hanns, parliamentary secretary to the minister for energy and decarbonisation.

“It’s hard to fathom how shocking it is that someone would do this to a tree believed to be about 500 years old, particularly in a national park,” the statement continues.

“Western Australians love this tree. Our community will be heartbroken, and they have every right to be angry,” the statement adds.

Experts are assessing the tree’s condition, “but right now our focus is on giving it every possible chance of survival and finding those responsible,” the politicians said.

“Whoever did this has damaged something precious to all of us,” they added.

Surveillance cameras have been installed in the area, and the site remains closed, Swinbourn and Hanns said, urging people not to visit the site.

They called on anyone who knows anything to “come forward. Anyone capable of such a deliberate and callous act should be held accountable.”

Police officers say the incident occurred between Saturday and Sunday, and a silver Jeep was subsequently seen in the area, the Australian Broadcasting Corporation reported Friday. They said the car’s occupants may be able to assist with inquiries.

Peter Murphy, convenor of local conservation organization Preston Environment Group, told the public broadcaster that the incident made his “heart sink,” adding: “Looking at the damage on scene photographs … I fear it may have to actually come down.”

In a statement Friday, councillor Tyrrell Gardiner, president of the Shire of Dardanup local government, joined calls for those responsible to “be identified,” and expressed hope that the tree would survive.

“The King Jarrah is one of the most recognised natural landmarks on our doorstep and something many Dardanup residents have grown up visiting with family and friends,” he said.

“To see it deliberately damaged is distressing and unacceptable,” Gardiner added. “We hope the King Jarrah can recover from this damage and continue to stand as a symbol of the natural heritage that makes our region so special.”
